solutions.explanation:
The angles run from \(1^\circ\) through \(89^\circ\), so each angle has its complement in the list. Every tangent is positive and finite, so every logarithm is defined.

For an acute angle \(\theta\), complementary angles interchange the opposite and adjacent legs of a right triangle. Thus
\[
\sin(90^\circ-\theta)=\cos\theta,
\qquad
\cos(90^\circ-\theta)=\sin\theta,
\]
and consequently
\[
\tan\theta\tan(90^\circ-\theta)=1.
\]
By the logarithm product rule, each complementary pair contributes
\[
\log_{10}(\tan\theta)
+\log_{10}(\tan(90^\circ-\theta))
=\log_{10}1=0.
\]
Pair \(k^\circ\) with \((90-k)^\circ\) for \(k=1,2,\ldots,44\). These pairs use every angle exactly once except \(45^\circ\). Its contribution is \(\log_{10}(\tan45^\circ)=\log_{10}1=0\).

Therefore the sum is \(\boxed{0}\), choice \(\text{A}\).
solutions.title: Pair complementary angles
